move.title: A dough you stretch by hand
move.body: Pizza dough is a lean yeast dough: flour, water, yeast, salt, and olive oil. Today you'll bloom the yeast, knead the dough until it's smooth and springy, let it rise, and stretch it with your fingertips to fill a sheet pan. Sauce, cheese, and a very hot oven do the rest.

callback.body: Pita taught you to bloom yeast in warm water and knead a lean dough. Pizza uses nearly the same dough, stretched into one big crust instead of rolled into rounds.

why.title: Warm water, not hot
why.body: Yeast is alive. Water at 105 to 110°F wakes it up; water above about 130°F starts to kill it. The foam on top shows it's working.

why.title: Why knead
why.body: Kneading builds gluten, a stretchy net in the dough. The net traps the yeast's gas so the dough rises, and lets it stretch thin without tearing.

why.title: If it springs back, let it rest
why.body: Stretched gluten pulls back like a rubber band. Five minutes of rest relaxes it, and the dough stretches out and stays.

why.title: A very hot oven
why.body: At 475°F, the crust browns and crisps underneath before the cheese burns on top. A cooler oven gives a pale, soft crust.

wrong.fix: The water was too hot or the yeast was old. Start again with fresh yeast and water at 105 to 110°F.

wrong.sign: The dough won't stretch to the corners
wrong.fix: Leave it 5 minutes and stretch again. It doesn't have to reach the corners exactly.
Use less sauce next time, and bake on the lowest rack.

wrong.sign: The cheese browned before the crust
wrong.fix: Move the pan to the lowest rack for the last few minutes.

quiz.q: What water temperature wakes up the yeast?
quiz.explain: Above about 130°F starts to kill it.

choices: Gluten, a stretchy net that holds the gas
quiz.explain: That's what lets the dough rise and stretch.

quiz.q: What do you do when the dough keeps springing back?
choices: Let it rest 5 minutes, then stretch again
quiz.explain: The gluten relaxes as it rests.

steps.text: Warm the water in the measuring cup in the microwave for about 30 seconds. Stir it and check it with the thermometer. It should read 105 to 110°F.
steps.tip: Too hot? Let it sit a minute and check again.

steps.text: Pour the water into the large bowl. Stir in the sugar, then sprinkle the yeast over the top and leave it alone to bloom.
steps.look: A layer of foam on top, and it smells like bread.

steps.text: Add the flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon of the oil. Stir with the wooden spoon until it's a rough, shaggy dough.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. Raw flour can make you sick.

steps.text: Dust the counter with flour and turn the dough out. Knead it until it's smooth and springs back when you poke it.
steps.look: Smooth and a little tacky, and a poke fills back in.

steps.text: Rub 1 tablespoon of the oil around the bowl, put the dough in, and turn it to coat. Cover it with the towel and let it rise somewhere warm.
steps.look: Doubled. A floured finger pressed in leaves a dent that stays.

steps.text: Put a rack in the lowest position and heat the oven to 475°F. Rub the last tablespoon of oil over the sheet pan.
If you're using the pepper, cut it in half, pull out the seeds, and slice it into thin strips.
Put the dough on the oiled pan. Press it out from the middle with your fingertips, toward the edges and corners.
steps.tip: If it springs back, leave it 5 minutes and press again.

steps.text: Spread the sauce over the dough with the back of the spoon, leaving a ½-inch edge. Scatter the cheese, oregano, and pepper strips over it.
Bake the pizza until the cheese bubbles and the edges are golden brown.
steps.look: Bubbling cheese with brown spots, and a golden edge.

steps.text: With oven mitts, pull the pan out partway. Lift a corner with the spatula. The bottom should be golden brown. If it's pale, bake 3 more minutes.

target.look: Golden brown underneath, and bubbling cheese

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Let the pizza sit 5 minutes, then slide it onto the cutting board with the spatula and cut it into 12 squares.
steps.tip: The cheese is very hot. Let it sit before you bite in.

warm-water.text: Microwave the water for about 30 seconds. Check it with the thermometer: 105 to 110°F.
warm-water.tip: Too hot? Wait a minute and check again.

bloom.text: Pour it into the large bowl. Stir in the sugar. Sprinkle the yeast on top.
bloom.look: Foam on top, and it smells like bread.

mix.text: Add the flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon of oil. Stir with the wooden spoon until shaggy.
mix.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. Raw flour can make you sick.

knead.text: Flour the counter. Knead the dough: push it away, fold it back, and turn it.
knead.look: Smooth, and a poke springs back.

rise.text: Rub 1 tablespoon of oil in the bowl. Add the dough, cover it with the towel, and let it rise.

oven.text: An adult puts a rack at the bottom and heats the oven to 475°F. Rub the last oil on the pan.

stretch.text: Put the dough on the pan. Press it out from the middle with your fingertips.
stretch.tip: Springing back? Wait 5 minutes, then press again.

bake.text: An adult slides the pan onto the bottom rack. Bake until the cheese bubbles.
bake.look: Bubbling cheese and a golden edge.

check.text: With an adult, lift a corner with the spatula. The bottom should be golden brown.

target.look: Golden brown underneath, and bubbling cheese

cut.text: Turn off the oven. Let the pizza rest 5 minutes. An adult cuts it into 12 squares.
cut.tip: The cheese is very hot. Wait before you bite.

add.text: Spread the sauce with the back of the spoon. Leave a ½-inch edge bare.
add.look: A thin, even layer of sauce.

add.text: Sprinkle the cheese and oregano all over the sauce.
add.look: Cheese right out to the sauce’s edge.

move.title: Bloom it, knead it, stretch it
move.body: Pizza dough is a yeast dough: flour, water, yeast, salt, and oil. Today you'll wake up the yeast in warm water, knead the dough for 5 minutes, let it rise, and press it out on a pan. An adult handles the very hot oven with you.
